method: Reads only: ls, find, cat, sed, grep, wc, md5sum, strings, xxd, dd, du. No file under the data dir was written, deleted, or modified. Entity UUIDs were enumerated once into /tmp/rmspec_u.txt on the device's tmpfs, which is a disclosed write to volatile storage outside the data dir (see the disclosure block). BusyBox 1.36.1 applies: no GNU long options, so `sed -n 1,25p` instead of `head -25`, and `file`, `sqlite3`, and `python3` are NOT installed on the device.
disclosure: One scratch file was written to the device's tmpfs: /tmp/rmspec_u.txt (the list of the 42 entity UUIDs, used to drive the correlation loops). /tmp is tmpfs -- volatile, cleared on reboot, outside the data dir. It was not deleted, because deletion is equally forbidden. Zero writes to persistent storage and zero writes anywhere under the xochitl data dir: entry count was 201 at session start and 201 at session end.

Every SSH invocation appends dropbear and systemd records to the systemd journal, which lives on /var/log/journal -- an ext4 mount on the same /dev/mapper/home-encrypted-disk partition as /home, and it survives reboots. That is an unavoidable persistent side effect of reading over SSH at all, and it is stated here rather than claimed away.

claims.shape: A single hidden file literally named `.tree` (no UUID basename), 25179 bytes, Qt QDataStream binary. The authoritative manifest of what is ELIGIBLE for cloud sync.
header_layout: 0x00  uint32 BE 0x0000000c + ASCII magic "rM sync tree"
0x10  uint32 BE 0x00000008 + qint64 BE, milliseconds since epoch
0x1c  qint64 BE, MICROSECONDS since epoch -- NO length prefix. This field is the one a naive parser misses.
0x24  uint32 BE 0x00000046 (= 70 bytes) + UTF-16BE QString, 35 chars: the cloud account id, of the form 'google-oauth2|<21-digit subject>' (lowercase g). REDACTED, not reproduced here.
claims.entry_layout: Per entry: uint32 kind (observed value 3 on 100% of entries), uint32 pathlen, ASCII path, uint32 0x00000020, 32-byte SHA-256, then a 28-byte trailing block carrying a size and a qint64 mtime. 190-191 entries; the first entry's path is "." (the root). 191 * 28 = 5348 bytes of trailer, ~21% of the file.
claims.evidence: $ ssh remarkable 'ls -la $D/.tree' -> "-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 25179 Aug 28 21:49 .../.tree"; $ ssh remarkable 'xxd -l 48 $D/.tree' -> "00000000: 0000 000c 724d 2073 796e 6320 7472 6565  ....rM sync tree / 00000010: 0000 0008 0000 01a0 4a59 7379 0006 5a22  ........JYsy..Z\" / 00000020: 6d7e a829 0000 0046 0067 006f 006f 0067  m~.)...F.g.o.o.g". Reading the offsets: the u32 len=8 at 0x10 covers 0x14-0x1b, but the QString length prefix 0000 0046 is at 0x24, not 0x1c -- eight bytes at 0x1c-0x23 are an unprefixed field. Decoding both: 0x14 -> 1787957457273 ms; 0x1c -> 1787957458287657 us; both land at 21:49, matching the file mtime, and both advanced by the same wall-clock delta between two reads taken 23 minutes apart.

claims.shape: Memory comes from /proc/meminfo (MemTotal, MemAvailable, both in kB meaning 1024 bytes). Storage comes from df, but ONLY in POSIX form: `df -k` WRAPS its output on this device and `df -Pk` does not.
claims.wrapping_trap: The documents partition is /dev/mapper/home-encrypted-disk -- 31 characters, wider than BusyBox df's 20-character Filesystem column -- so `df -k` emits the device name on its own line and the six numeric fields on the NEXT line. Any parser doing `df -k ... | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}'` reads the wrong field, or none. BusyBox 1.36.1 supports -P: `Usage: df [-PkmhT] [-t TYPE] [FILESYSTEM]...`, and -P puts all six fields on one line.
claims.evidence: $ ssh remarkable 'sed -n 1,6p /proc/meminfo' -> "MemTotal: 2009400 kB / MemFree: 1224912 kB / MemAvailable: 1251016 kB / Buffers: 7884 kB / Cached: 111252 kB / SwapCached: 0 kB". $ ssh remarkable 'df -k /home/root/.local/share/remarkable/xochitl' -> "Filesystem           1K-blocks      Used Available Use% Mounted on" then "/dev/mapper/home-encrypted-disk" alone on line 2 then "                      48568796    112564  47929504   0% /home" on line 3. $ ssh remarkable 'df -Pk /home/root/.local/share/remarkable/xochitl' -> header then "/dev/mapper/home-encrypted-disk             48568796    112564  47929504   0% /home" on ONE line; field-splitting that line with `while read a b c d e f` yields exactly "[/dev/mapper/home-encrypted-disk][48568796][112564][47929504][0%][/home]". $ ssh remarkable 'df --help' -> "BusyBox v1.36.1 () multi-call binary. / Usage: df [-PkmhT] [-t TYPE] [FILESYSTEM]...".
claims.arithmetic: Blocks are 1024 bytes, so total = 48568796 * 1024 and available = 47929504 * 1024. Used + Available < total because of reserved blocks (112564 + 47929504 = 48042068 against 48568796), so a reading satisfies an available <= total invariant without the two ever being an identity. Do not derive total from Used + Available.
claims.notes: Neither `free` nor a `du` walk is needed for either gauge, which is what the legacy tree shelled out to and string-parsed. Passing the xochitl data directory itself to df -Pk resolves to the /home mount, so the caller never has to know the mount point.

The reMarkable DEVICE serial has NONE that is readable without touching a forbidden file. /sys/devices/soc0/serial_number and /proc/device-tree/serial-number both exist and both hold 16 characters, but that is the i.MX8MM SoC unique id -- a different fact from the RM02A-form serial the tablet UI shows.
claims.evidence: $ ssh remarkable 'for f in family machine machine_id revision soc_id; do printf "%s=" $f; cat /sys/devices/soc0/$f; done' -> "family=Freescale i.MX / machine=reMarkable Ferrari / machine_id=<32 hex chars, withheld> / revision=1.0 / soc_id=i.MX8MM"; $ ssh remarkable 'ls -A /sys/devices/soc0' -> "family machine machine_id power revision serial_number soc_id subsystem uevent"; both serial paths report `wc -c` = 17 (16 characters plus a terminator), value withheld. $ ssh remarkable 'ls -A /home/root/.config/remarkable/' -> "csl.conf memfault_project_key.conf wifi_networks.conf xochitl.conf" (names only; nothing opened). Existence probes: /etc/remarkable.conf absent, /usr/share/remarkable/update.conf absent, /home/root/.config/remarkable/serial absent, /sys/class/dmi/id/product_serial absent.

sources.firmware: IMG_VERSION in /etc/os-release -> "3.27.3.0". /etc/version holds the build stamp "20260612085811", which is not what a user recognises as a firmware version.
sources.serial: NO clean source. The RM02A-form serial appears only in /home/root/.config/remarkable/xochitl.conf, which no source file in this workspace may reference (tests/architecture/test_secret_containment.py), and in rm.user.auth.cli journal lines, which GET /log.txt redacts.

claims.consequence: A DeviceFacts.serial reported from /sys/devices/soc0/serial_number would be a different fact wearing the right field's name. The field belongs in DeviceFacts.unsupported for BOTH transports, and the reason is structural -- the only sources are a file this workspace is forbidden to reference and a redacted log -- not a transient read failure.
claims.notes: Also newly noted: /usr/share/remarkable/update.conf, which the legacy tree's DevicePaths.UPDATE_CONF names as the firmware-version source, DOES NOT EXIST on this firmware. Any code reading it gets nothing.

claims.shape: Userland is BusyBox 1.36.1. NO GNU long options. `file`, `sqlite3` and `python3` are NOT installed. `od`, `hexdump`, `xxd`, `strings`, `dd`, `find`, `md5sum` ARE.
claims.evidence: $ ssh remarkable 'strings /usr/share/remarkable/webui/assets/index.js | ... | head -40' -> "head: invalid option -- '4' / BusyBox v1.36.1 () multi-call binary. / Usage: head [OPTIONS] [FILE]..."; prior session: $ command -v file -> MISSING; $ command -v sqlite3 -> MISSING; $ command -v python3 -> MISSING.
claims.notes: Use `sed -n 1,25p` not `head -25`. Use `sed -n 1,20p` for tails too, or `tail -N` (short form works). Any script that shells out to sqlite3 on the device will fail; read the .db header with dd + xxd + strings instead, or copy it off (and disclose that you did).

refuted.claim: .metadata has two schema generations: a modern/slim 10-key set on 28 docs and a legacy/fat 15-key set on 14 docs.
refuted.observation: SEVEN key sets, not two. The claimed modern 10-key set matches only 13 files: all 5 folders lack lastOpened and lastOpenedPage, and 15 of the 28 sync-free files lack new/source. new+source is not a generation marker at all -- it appears on 27 files spanning both generations (13 modern docs + 12 legacy docs + 2 folders). createdTime is 41 of 42, not universal: c0956d61 lacks it. And the original grep pattern \"modified\" cannot match the key metadatamodified, so that field was never actually tested.
refuted.correction: See claim file-type:.metadata. Field names, spellings and the type enum were all correct; the field-to-file mapping was not.

refuted.claim: .content has ~48 top-level keys on a notebook, including cPages, pages, pageCount, verticalScroll, scrollTime, LastPen, SecondaryPen, first, second, idx, id, timestamp, uuids, value, original, template, lastOpened.
refuted.observation: Off by roughly 2x, and it mixes nesting levels. The cited notebook has 23 top-level keys; the range across all 40 files is 22-24 for documents, 1 for collections, 5 for one minified legacy PDF; the union of top-level keys across all 40 is 26. Of the names listed, 27 are NESTED: the 14 Last*/Secondary* fields live under extraMetadata, and pages/uuids/lastOpened/original/first/second/id/idx/template/timestamp/value/scrollTime/verticalScroll live under cPages or deeper. The claim's own evidence command was a flat any-depth grep, which cannot distinguish top-level from nested. That same command also silently dropped 21 real keys containing digits (all *v2* extraMetadata fields): the true any-depth distinct count is 71, not 48 or 50.
refuted.correction: See claim file-type:.content. The claim also omitted three real top-level keys: dummyDocument (2 files), keyboardMetadata (1 file), and margins as optional (17 of 40). formatVersion, the CollectionType degenerate {"tags":[]} form, and the contentFormatVersion note were all correct.

refuted.claim: .pagedata holds one line per page naming that page's background template, superseded by .content cPages[].template.
refuted.observation: Three failures. (1) Not one line per page: d3b38661 has pageCount 432 and 432 cPages entries against a 1-line, 6-byte .pagedata. (2) The line does not name the page's template: 2cf3200e's .pagedata says 'Blank' while its single page's template.value is 'P Grid small'. (3) Nothing supersedes it on that PDF: d3b38661's 143 KB .content contains ZERO "template" keys, and 16 of 40 .content files have no template key at all.
refuted.correction: Both files hold a stale default 'Blank' line independent of page count or real template. Treat .pagedata as optional and non-authoritative; read cPages.pages[].template.value (a timestamped {timestamp, value} pair, itself optional). Also refuted: the claim's premise that 'both are 1-page-equivalent' -- d3b38661 is 432 pages. And 'legacy' is wrong: d3b38661 was created 2026-03-08 on current firmware.

refuted.claim: 194 .rm files, all v6 CRDT scene binaries; pages with no ink have no file.
refuted.observation: The count and the path template are exact, but 86 of the 194 are exactly 0 bytes and carry no v6 header -- rmscene raises EOFError on them. And 'no ink means no file' is false: all 86 zero-byte files sit inside the 12 .failure documents, which have one 0-byte .rm per page id in .content despite zero ink (31ec7d01: 10 pages, 10 .rm, all empty).
refuted.correction: 108 v6 scene files plus 86 zero-byte placeholders. A page has three possible states, and a parser must stat-and-skip zero-length files. See claim file-type:.rm.

refuted.claim: .tree layout is: uint32 len + magic, then uint32 0x08 + an 8-byte block, then the account-id QString, then length-prefixed path strings each followed by a binary hash.
refuted.observation: The header is short by 8 bytes and the entry shape is short by two fields. Following the stated sequence puts the QString length prefix at 0x1c, where the value is 0x00065a21 = 416289 -- a 416 KB read from a 25179-byte file, i.e. immediate parse failure on byte 4. There is an UNPREFIXED qint64 microsecond-epoch field at 0x1c-0x23 that the claim omits; the QString prefix is at 0x24. Each entry also carries a leading uint32 kind (=3) before the path length, and a 28-byte trailer after the hash holding a size and an mtime -- 191*28 = 5348 bytes, 21% of the file, undescribed. The root entry with path "." is also missing from the claim's path list.
refuted.correction: See claim file-type:.tree. The magic, size, path classes and length prefixes, the 99/30/28/2/1 extension counts, 30 roots, and the zero-mentions-of-.local/.failure/.thumbnails findings all reproduce exactly. Separately: the account id prefix is lowercase 'google-oauth2|' (an Auth0 connection name), not 'Google-oauth2|' -- the claim's own hex gutter (".g.o.o.g.l.e") already contradicted its prose.

refuted.claim: The xochitl data dir holds ~200 entries.
refuted.observation: Exactly 201, and the inventory omitted the .tree file entirely.
refuted.correction: See claim census:201-entries. Reproduced twice, four months apart in the journal window.

refuted.claim: Read-only discipline: 2 scratch files written to on-device tmpfs; zero writes to persistent storage.
refuted.observation: The data-dir cleanliness holds (201 entries before and after), but 'zero writes to persistent storage' cannot. Every SSH invocation appends dropbear and systemd records to the systemd journal, which is a rw ext4 mount on /dev/mapper/home-encrypted-disk -- the same encrypted partition as /home -- and survives reboots. A prior session also undercounted its own tmpfs footprint by an order of magnitude and asserted 'zero HTTP requests' in a window that contained 96 rm.usb.web lines.
refuted.correction: The honest statement is: zero writes under the data dir, zero writes to persistent storage OTHER than the journal records our own SSH logins unavoidably create, and N disclosed scratch files on tmpfs. See the disclosure block at the top of this file.
